tools.name: create_draft
tools.description:
Creates a new draft email in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool takes recipient addresses (`to`, `cc`, `bcc`), a `subject`, and body content as inputs. Plain text body content can be provided in `body` (do NOT format `body` with Markdown), and rich-text HTML content can be provided in `htmlBody` (use valid HTML tags for formatting; if both are provided, `body` serves as the plain-text alternative). If the draft is created as a reply to an existing message, the ID of the original message should be passed to the tool in the `replyToMessageId` field. Set `includeSignature` to true to append the user's configured Gmail web signature to the draft.

Returns a Draft object with the `id`, `threadId`, and `viewUrl` fields populated.

Attachment.description: Represents an attachment to be included in an email.

content.description: Required. The base64-encoded content of the attachment.

filename.description: Optional. The name of the file to be attached, e.g. "invoice.pdf". Email clients show this name to recipients for both regular and inline attachments. If not provided, the attachment may be received with no name.

id.description: Optional. Output only. When present, contains the ID of an external attachment that can be retrieved in a separate `GetMessageAttachment` request.

inline.description: Optional. If `true`, this attachment is handled as inline. An inline attachment is content, such as an image, that is displayed within the body of an HTML email instead of being listed as a separate file for download. To display an inline attachment, add `` to `html_body`, where `` is the attachment's zero-based position in `attachments`, counting all attachments. For example, if `attachments` contains a PDF followed by an inline PNG, use `` for the PNG. Don't reference inline attachments by `filename`. Other images in `html_body` are removed. If `false` or absent, defaults to `false`, and it's treated as a regular attachment.

mimeType.description: Optional. The field representing a content or media type must use IANA MIME type, https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml. If not provided, defaults to "application/octet-stream".

attachments.description: Optional. The attachments to include in the email. The combined size of attachments in the message cannot exceed 25MB. If you need to send files larger than 25MB, upload the file to Drive first and then insert the Drive link into `body` or `html_body`.

bcc.description: Optional. The blind carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

body.description: Optional. The plain text body content of the email draft. Do NOT format this field with Markdown (such as headers `#`, bold `**`, bullet points `*`, or tables `|`). If formatted rich text is desired, use `html_body` instead. If `html_body` is also provided, this field is treated as the plain-text alternative.

cc.description: Optional. The carbon copy recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

htmlBody.description: Optional. The HTML content of the email draft. If provided, this will be used as the rich-text version of the email.

includeSignature.description: Optional. Whether to append the user's configured Gmail web signature to the draft. Defaults to false.

replyToMessageId.description: Optional. The ID of the message to reply to. If provided, this will be used as the reply-to message ID for the email draft, and the `body` and `html_body` will be appended to the original message body.

subject.description: Optional. The subject line of the email. Defaults to empty if not provided.

to.description: Optional. The primary recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com").

Optional comments can be added before the forwarded message using `forwardText` for plain text (do NOT format with Markdown) or `htmlBody` for rich HTML. Set `includeSignature` to true to append the user's configured Gmail web signature to the forwarded message.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description:
Lists draft emails from the authenticated user's Gmail account, optionally filtered by a query string.

Note: An empty JSON object `{}` represents zero matching items, not an error.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of drafts to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. A token received from a previous `list_drafts` call to retrieve the next page of results. Leave empty to fetch the first page.

query.description: Optional. A query string to filter the drafts. Natural language queries must be pre-converted into Gmail compatible syntax queries to use this tool. If omitted, all drafts (excluding spam and trash by default) are listed. The tool inherently only searches for drafts. Supported operators include `from:`, `to:`, `cc:`, `bcc:`, `after:YYYY/MM/DD`, `before:YYYY/MM/DD`, `older_than:`, `newer_than:`, `subject:`, `has:`, `filename:`, `""` (exact phrase), `label:` (display name), `in:`, `is:`, `larger:`, `smaller:`, `AND`, `OR`, `-` (exclude) and `( )` (grouping). Examples: `subject:OneMCP Update`, `to:gduser2@workspacesamples.dev AND newer_than:7d`, `is:unread`.

view.description: Optional. Controls the fields populated for drafts in the draft list. Defaults to returning metadata only (`id`, `thread_id`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`). Set to `DRAFT_VIEW_FULL` to include `subject` and `plaintext_body` content.

Returns full draft content, including `subject` and `plaintext_body` in addition to draft metadata (if applicable).

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: Lists all labels available in the authenticated user's Gmail account. Use this tool to discover the `labelId` and display `name` of each label in `labels` before calling `label_thread`, `unlabel_thread`, `label_message`, or `unlabel_message`. Note: the system labels, `DRAFT` and `SENT`, cannot be set on messages and are read only.

tools.name: mark_thread_spam
tools.description:
Marks an entire thread as Spam in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread.

Use `mark_thread_spam` when marking a thread as spam, even if it currently contains only 1 message. Marking spam at the thread level ensures all current messages in the thread are marked as Spam.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to mark as Spam.

tools.name: search_threads
tools.description:
Lists email threads from the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This tool can filter threads based on a query string and supports pagination. It returns a list of threads, each with its thread `id`, `messageCount` (total messages in the thread), `viewUrl`, and a subset of up to 5 related messages (each with its own message `id`, `viewUrl`, `sender`, recipients, `date`, and `labelIds`). Use this tool to find thread `id`s matching a query before reading full threads or performing actions on matching emails or threads. The `view` parameter controls which additional fields are populated in the returned message subset. By default (or with `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`), it includes `subject` and `snippet`. Use `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` to exclude `subject` and `snippet`. Full message bodies, attachment metadata, and messages beyond the 5-message subset are not returned by this tool; use the 'get_thread' tool with a thread ID to retrieve all messages (and their message IDs) in a thread or to fetch full message bodies.

includeTrash.description: Optional. Include threads from TRASH in the results. Defaults to false.

pageSize.description: Optional. The maximum number of threads to return. If unspecified, defaults to 20. The maximum allowed value is 50.

pageToken.description: Optional. Page token to retrieve a specific page of results in the list. Leave empty to fetch the first page.

query.description: Optional. A query string to filter the threads. Natural language queries must be pre-converted into Gmail syntax queries to use this tool. If omitted, all threads (excluding spam and trash by default) are listed. Supported operators include `from:`, `to:`, `cc:`, `bcc:`, `after:YYYY/MM/DD`, `before:YYYY/MM/DD`, `older_than:`, `newer_than:`, `subject:`, `has:`, `filename:`, `""` (exact phrase), `label:` (display name), `category:`, `in:`, `is:`, `larger:`, `smaller:`, `AND`, `OR`, `-` (exclude) and `( )` (grouping). Examples: `subject:OneMCP Update`, `from:user@example.com`, `to:user2@example.com AND newer_than:7d`, `project proposal has:attachment`, `is:unread -in:sent`. Favor concise, keyword-based queries over long subject strings or full sentences.

view.description: Optional. Controls the fields populated for threads in the thread list. Defaults to `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL`. `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL` returns `id`, `snippet`, `subject`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`, `view_url` (if applicable). `THREAD_VIEW_METADATA_ONLY` returns `id`, `sender`, `to_recipients`, `cc_recipients`, `bcc_recipients`, `date`, `label_ids`, `view_url` (if applicable). `THREAD_VIEW_IDS_ONLY` returns only `id` on each `Thread` without fetching per-thread message metadata. `THREAD_VIEW_SUMMARY` returns `THREAD_VIEW_MINIMAL` fields with only the most recent message per thread (`messages` has at most 1 entry), plus `message_count` and `view_url` on the thread.

tools.name: trash_message
tools.description:
Moves a specific message to the Trash (soft delete) in the authenticated user's Gmail account.

This is the default tool (along with `trash_thread`) when a user asks to 'delete', 'remove', or 'get rid of' a message without explicitly requesting permanent, irreversible deletion. Use `trash_message` when targeting a specific message within a thread. To trash an entire thread or a single-message thread, prefer `trash_thread`.

To find the message ID, use the `get_thread` tool. To find the draft message ID, use tools like `list_drafts`.

messageId.description: Required. The ID of the message to move to Trash.

tools.name: trash_thread
tools.description:
Moves an entire thread to the Trash (soft delete) in the authenticated user's Gmail account. This operation affects all messages currently in the thread.

This is the default tool (along with `trash_message`) when a user asks to 'delete', 'remove', or 'get rid of' an email or thread without explicitly requesting permanent, irreversible deletion. Use `trash_thread` when trashing a thread, even if it currently contains only 1 message. Trashing at the thread level ensures all current messages in the thread are moved to Trash.

threadId.description: Required. The ID of the thread to move to Trash.

Use `unlabel_thread` when removing labels from an email or thread (such as marking it as read by removing `UNREAD`, archiving it by removing `INBOX`, or removing user-defined labels), even if the thread currently contains only 1 message. threadId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the thread to remove labels from.

draftId.description: Required. The unique identifier of the draft to update.

htmlBody.description: Optional. The HTML content of the email draft. If provided, this will be used as the rich-text version of the email.

subject.description: Optional. The subject line of the email. If omitted or empty, the existing subject is preserved.

to.description: Optional. The primary recipients of the email draft. Each string MUST be a valid plain email address (e.g., "user@example.com"). If omitted or empty, the existing recipients are preserved.
